title: Session-aware prefix summarization and KV slimming to improve GPU memory headroom
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Problem:
Current KV/prefix cache stores complete token sequences for many short-lived prompts. Under sustained multi-tenant load this leads to GPU memory pressure and frequent slab compaction that increases GC pauses and raises tail latency. Continuous batching increases reuse opportunities but also aggregates many unique small prefixes into the GPU cache, exacerbating memory fragmentation.

Proposal summary:
Introduce a session-aware prefix summarization layer that creates compact, lossy summaries for low-reuse prefixes and maintains full KV entries only for high-reuse hot prefixes. The system will: 
1) Track prefix reuse heat in a short session window (per-tenant and global), using an approximate counter (count-min / hot list).
2) For prefixes below a reuse threshold, replace the stored KV sequence with a compressed "summary" that:
   - stores the minimal set of KV frames required to reconstruct equivalent hidden-state output for the next N tokens (heuristic N=8),
   - uses quantized representation (8-bit) and optional delta-encoding across adjacent layers,
   - includes a small reconstruction hint (seed, minimal prompt-slice) to rehydrate on-demand.
3) Opportunistic deduplication: identify near-identical suffixes across prefixes via locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) and coalesce their shared KV frames into a shared slab reference to reduce duplication across tenants/requests.
4) Background compaction thread: periodically scans low-heat summaries and attempts to merge or evict according to current GPU memory headroom and SLO budget. Compaction pauses if observed P95 token latency exceeds the configured threshold.
5) Continuous batching integration: ensure summaries are compatible with batched KV composition by exposing a lightweight reconstruction API that can run on the CPU or on a warm GPU stream to rehydrate only when the batch includes a request that benefits from it.

Why different from existing approaches:
- Instead of purely evict/retain heuristics, this uses a lossy-but-fast rehydration strategy to trade a small compute cost for large memory savings.
- Session-windowed heat counters emphasize temporal locality (recent reuse) which fits chat-like workloads where prefixes recur within a session but not globally.
- LSH-based coalescing targets cross-request similarity rather than exact fingerprint dedupe, reducing near-duplicate storage across paraphrases and templated prompts.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- Reduce average KV memory footprint across production GPU pools by >= 18% under the chat workload benchmark (measured on runtime-1.22 staging cluster).
- No more than +3% increase in median token latency and no more than +8% increase in P95 token latency on canary for a 5-minute window post-deploy.
- Rehydration path keeps CPU-to-GPU transfer times minimal: average rehydration time per rehydrate op < 1.5 ms on warm stream, and <6 ms cold.
- End-to-end functional tests that validate fidelity: sampling responses after rehydration differ by <1% token-level divergence on a curated eval set compared to baseline full-KV path.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Design doc and perf model (DONE) - link in attachments.
2) Heat tracker + policy service (server-side): implement approximate counters, heat buckets, and policy evaluation for summary conversion (2w).
3) Summary encoding on write path: implement quantized summary format and serialization to slab store (2w).
4) LSH coalescer: batch offline and online similarity detection with cold-start bloom filter to avoid high false positives (1.5w).
5) Rehydration API & batching compatibility: CPU and GPU warm-stream rehydrate; add hooks to continuous batching runtime (2w).
6) Background compactor and safety throttle (1w).
7) End-to-end benchmarks + canary rollout (1.5w).

Rollout strategy:
- Feature-flag gated: enable KV-slimming off by default.
- Canary groups: 1% internal traffic -> 5% staging -> 20% load test -> 100% if P95 and memory targets met.
- Safety kill-switch: immediate disable if P95 regression > 12% or error rate increases above baseline by 2x.

Open design trade-offs / risks:
- Lossy summaries could introduce quality regressions for long-horizon prompts; mitigated by session heat threshold and acceptance fidelity tests.
- LSH false positives may cause incorrect coalescing; use conservative thresholds and attach provenance to shared slabs for quick rollback.
- Additional CPU/GPU ops for rehydration may affect tail latency under spikes; we throttle rehydrate concurrency and leverage warm-stream reuse.

Testing / validation:
- Microbenchmarks for rehydrate hot/cold paths (latency and bandwidth).
- End-to-end chat workload replay on staging: measure memory, latency, and output divergence.
- AB test: responses scored by quality eval harness on curated prompts to catch semantic regressions.

Next steps / immediate tasks (owner in parentheses):
- Attach detailed perf model and storage format spec to this ticket (Aisha Patel).
- Implement heat-tracker prototype and expose metrics (Riley Chen).
- Create perf dashboard in Grafana for memory headroom, rehydrate ops per second, and P95 latency (Infra SRE).
- Create unit + integration tests for summary encode/decode (Eng QA).

Notes on compatibility and data retention:
- Summaries and coalesced slabs include TTL tied to session windows; they are considered ephemera and do not change long-term audit logs.
- For Private/VPC deployments, provide an opt-out flag to disable cross-tenant slab sharing; LSH coalescing will be limited to tenant-local space to respect isolation.
